4.5 Making a Complaint About the University’s Handling of Personal Information
4.5.1 If an individual wishes to make a complaint about the University’s handling of personal
information he or she should contact the Legal Office of the relevant Campus. The
Legal Office will try to resolve the matter informally.
4.5.2 If a complaint cannot be resolved, the individual will be required to formally lodge the
complaint in writing to the Legal Office with any supporting documentation attached to
the complaint.
4.5.3 The University will deal with the complaint within 30 business days and advise the
individual lodging the complaint of the outcome.
4.5.4 If the individual is unhappy with the outcome he or she may refer the complaint to the
Office of the Australian Information Commissioner. Further information about the
external dispute resolution can be found at www.oaic.gov.au.

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Authorised AI assessment contributions, accountable human group responsibility and protection of group personal information.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: N028 (4.5.2.3, 4.5.2.5) prohibits unauthorised AI-modified submissions and unauthorised distribution/file-sharing, N026 (6.2.1.1) requires identifiable individual group contributions, and N035 (6.1.17) protects others' rights.
case_summary.case_note: Policy: Academic Integrity (N028, 4.5.2.3, 4.5.2.5) and Procedure: Assessment and Examinations (N026, 6.2.1.1) prohibit unauthorised generative AI contributions and file-sharing while requiring identifiable individual group contributions. However, intra-group consent for connecting AI agents to shared workspaces holding members' personal details is not specifically regulated; Protocol v1.1 critical-risk criteria were adopted after preliminary review.
